blurb: A young reporter joins the fierce Professor Challenger on a journey to a plateau in South America where dinosaurs still live.
source: The Lost World by Arthur Conan Doyle (1912). Read it in your own copy, or borrow it free from your library.

streets.name: Professor Challenger
streets.blurb: Young Malone wants to do something heroic. His editor sends him to interview the famous — and furious — Professor Challenger.
streets.how: Professor Challenger does NOT like reporters! Run down the street before he catches you.

streets.name: The Meeting
streets.blurb: At a noisy scientific meeting, Challenger dares anyone to go and check his story. Malone stands up.
streets.how: The hall is full of shouts! Catch the volunteers’ hands going up — and dodge the flying heckles.

params.done: “I will go!” — Malone joins the expedition.

streets.name: Up the Amazon
streets.blurb: Two canoes, two professors — one in each, to keep the peace — paddling up a dark, clear river.
streets.how: Paddle the canoe upriver. Pick up the supplies and steer clear of the logs and rocks.

params.done: Through the bamboo, and the red cliffs are in sight.

streets.name: The Plateau
streets.blurb: Red cliffs too steep to climb — but beside them stands a tall pinnacle of rock with one tree on top.
streets.how: Climb the rock pinnacle to the tree at the top. Then work out how to cross to the plateau.

params.objective: Reach the top of the pinnacle

solve.prompt: How can the party cross the gap to the plateau?
options: Chop down the tree on the pinnacle so it falls across as a bridge
Wait for the pterodactyl to carry them
solve.hint: What did Challenger carry up with him?

params.done: The tree crashes across the gap — a bridge to the unknown!

streets.name: The Pterodactyls
streets.blurb: The explorers stumble on a rookery full of pterodactyls — and the whole flock takes to the air.
streets.how: Run through the swamp and get back under the trees before the wings close in!

streets.name: The Iguanodons
streets.blurb: Malone climbs the tallest tree on the plateau to see the whole of Maple White Land.
streets.how: Explore the glade and find six specimens and landmarks for the map.

params.label: found
params.objective: Find the landmarks for the map

finale.say: Remarkable. Iguanodons — harmless, and quite alive! Note everything down, young man.

streets.name: Captured
streets.blurb: Malone comes back from a night alone to find the camp empty. Lord John has escaped — and the two professors must be rescued.
streets.how: Creep with Lord John through the forest to the professors. Keep out of sight of the ape-men’s lookouts.

streets.name: The Way Down
streets.blurb: A young friend from the plateau gives Malone a roll of bark with a secret drawing on it.
streets.how: Look at the clues in the camp, then work out which cave leads down to the outside world.

clues.label: The roll of bark
clues.text: A row of dots for the caves, with a cross by one of them. The young friend pointed up at the caves and put his finger to his lips.

clues.label: Challenger’s balloon
clues.text: Challenger’s homemade balloon shot up and nearly carried two of them off. Not a safe way down!

clues.label: The wrong cave
clues.text: The first cave they tried ended in a wall of rock. Were they counting from the wrong end?

solve.label: The cave
solve.prompt: Why did they reach a dead end the first time?
options: They counted the caves from the wrong side of the drawing
The cave had been blocked by the Professor
solve.hint: Seventeen from one end is second from the other.

skyRun.name: The Rookery Cliffs
skyRun.blurb: up the red cliffs above the pterodactyl rookery.
skyRun.how: Climb the ledges of the red cliffs to the very top. Some ledges move — wait for them!

params.objective: Reach the top of the cliffs

npcs.name: Professor Summerlee
npcs.idle: I shall believe in Maple White Land when I see it with my own eyes.
npcs.thanks: Splendid notes! Even Challenger will be impressed.

steps.text: Talk to Professor Summerlee by the plateau gate.
steps.say: My specimen notes have blown out of my case! Six pages — beetles, ferns, flowers. Science cannot do without them.

steps.text: Find six pages of Summerlee’s notes.
Bring the notes back to Summerlee.
steps.say: All six! Now we shall have proof that nobody can argue with.

vault.name: The Queen’s Hall
vault.blurb: an escape room in the packed Queen’s Hall: prove the Lost World is real to a hall full of doubters.
vault.intro: The Queen’s Hall is packed and the doubters are shouting. Open three locks to prove that Maple White Land is real.

stations.label: The evidence table
stations.text: The doubters say photographs can be faked. Which kind of proof can nobody argue with?
stations.lesson: Good scientists ask for evidence — and the best evidence is something everyone can see for themselves.

solve.prompt: What will convince the whole hall?
options: A living creature from the plateau, there in the hall
solve.hint: What did Challenger bring in a big box?

stations.label: The four explorers
stations.text: Match each explorer to what they did.
stations.lesson: Four very different people — and each one mattered.

pairs: Doubted him and came to check
Led the rescue of the professors
Climbed the great tree and wrote it all down

quiz.label: Malone’s notebook
quiz.lesson: From a newspaper office in London to the top of Maple White Land and back.

vault.openText: The lid of the box lifts — and something with leathery wings looks out.
vault.outro: The pterodactyl escapes through an open window and flies off over London. But the hall has seen it with its own eyes.
